results.translated_text: Haci lady! + I wish you all the best for your trip. Thank you so much for everything. Unfortunately, the various authors didn't want us to see each other before your departure. Nevertheless, I will try to do fruitful work for you. 7. Uler evening. Yours, Bob. And Solben, I received the approval for the plane ticket. rs I have Peats, haugh & Art, depending on whether I have Peatz. So I'll definitely come to Pemptens. Yours, Bob. p. 1.38 Zabūs, your letter finally arrived last night. However, I can't understand why you couldn't get any mail for 10 days. Besides, I always wrote immediately when I knew something definite. = Little one, I won't complain anymore, but if this goes on for days, I'm ready for a sanatorium. It's a shame that so much valuable energy is wasted. The 3-day journey didn't bother me at all. I still need three visas: Hungary, Yugoslavia, and Switzerland. The Yugoslavian one was rejected yesterday, so I have to submit it in Belgrade, and that takes days. In my desperation, I called the Foreign Ministry again. Dr. From called today and I was told he'd come back. I went there immediately, spoke with his representative, we had another phone consultation, and now I'm sitting downstairs in the Finance Ministry waiting for the letter they'll give me for the National Bank. So I'm making one more attempt to get the plane ticket approved! Zabūs, you'll only be able to understand all of this when I tell you everything in person. It couldn't be more complicated. What you know is at most 10% of it. I'm handling it all personally. It's nerve-wracking. Do you know how happy I'd be if I could just put all this behind me?! You can be sure I'm doing everything I can. Sure, I've made mistakes, but if you knew everything beforehand... Regarding Troc's letter, the telegram I sent regarding my visit today has of course become irrelevant due to the letter. Little one, please don't be impatient; I'm already impatient enough. His Zob.

results.translated_text: Prague, January 23, 1936. Babus, it was truly a great joy you gave me with the photos. I had to look at them again and again because you received them. Some really turned out beautifully. Unfortunately, it was an unforgivable mistake on my part with most of the pictures, despite using Pan film with a self-disc camera. As a result, many very nice little details were lost. Next time, something like that shouldn't happen again. The films have arrived in the meantime, but there is still some excellent material available. You still have some. In any case, you'll get good things. Anyway, I would never have thought that Zaba could be so pretty – of course, only in pictures. Is that thanks to the girl, the photos, or the photographer? – Let's talk about the photos. Thank you so much, my dear. Otherwise, my birthday went very nicely and with presents. Many things, including gramophone records, shirts, towel fabric, shawls, ties, perfume, etc. Yes, Ellen, a wonderful Montblanc fountain pen, and diligently crafted items, all in a case with a very nice letter. She only mentions my last letter very briefly, in which she considers part of it tasteless. But she didn't take it. In the summer, she's going to Palestine. Today I was at the Elekta Film Company, Prague 1, Narodny tr. 26. (Mr. Auerbach) He was very nice and will look through the book. He would have preferred it in German, but he left. If you have any free time, send it to me or him. He also wants to send it to Berlin. He told me that I should contact various film producers. Well, we'll see. I have two more people here to whom I would like to show the book. I am, of course, leaving all decisions regarding possible film rights to them. I am also sending the attached photos. Write to me soon about how things are going: how you're doing and how it's going. Lots of love. I'll send the film back in three weeks when I no longer need it. Elisabeth Aigner, Paris 15th arrondissement, 6.9 bis Rue Grancion, Prague 13th arrondissement, Ruska
